title: Stepin Fetchit as master of psychology
summary: Butler calls Stepin Fetchit a psychologist who gave white audiences the slow, dumb act and used it to profit, robbing gamblers in his dressing room.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, did you know Stepen Fetchit?
Yeah, Stepen Fetchit is a master of psychology. I think he went to McGill University in Canada. Oh, Stepen Fetchit, same type of man. Same type of man.
Why do you think he hit upon his type approach?

Well, because it was the period, man, where those naturals -- but I'm right there with them, there's something about them that fascinates me. Stepen Fetchit told me, said, "Jacques," one day when I was talking to some friend -- no, we were having a meeting somewhere (talking.1e). And we had a cat. And the cat started walking across the floor, across the room, slow, with its tail up there, and everybody (stopped.1e) In other words, what is he doing, are you talking to me? And he says, go on, cat, get off of there. And the cat stopped and said Meow, and kept looking around. (Inaudible). I guess, in other words, "Now?" "Yeah. Now, get out of here!"

So he said, now, he thought of that. And when Will Rogers was making a picture and he was grousing about he wasn't in a job; he got a broom. And he got a man did that cat manuver. (inaudible), "Boss, what do you mean?" (inaudible) because they wanted to see a man of color give them what they wanted, that slow, dumb, slow-moving nigger. So he gave them just what they wanted.

So as long as Will Rogers was alive, he was in there. And all of America just loved it, just ate it up. Ate it up. Lackadaisical; so lazy. (Inaudible). And he was another one that was slick. He always had his -- name was Lincoln Perry, I think. All had beautiful cars, beautiful women. When they get famous, doing what he was doing, you'd better not be trying to talk him out of that stuff, man. You dare not.

And you know, on the shows, all these people loved to gamble. Stepen Fetchit used to have a dressing room, have all kinds of biscuits for the boys, and they would come there to get him. And he would rob them every week. I was on the show with him for about 31 weeks and he robbed them 31 weeks. And I said, "Stepen" he said, "What, do you say, Jack. If they want it, And so I give them the pleasure of trying. (Inaudible)."
